points.title: 童年与少年时期
points.description: C.S.刘易斯出生于爱尔兰贝尔法斯特的一个新教家庭，父亲是律师，母亲早逝。童年时期展现出非凡的想象力，经常与哥哥一起创作故事。1908年进入坎特伯里寄宿学校，后于1911年进入马尔文学院。这一时期他经历了宗教信仰的丧失，开始质疑基督教教义。1917年，他考入牛津大学，但第一次世界大战爆发后，他自愿加入英国军队，被派往法国前线服役。
points.descriptionEn: C.S. Lewis was born in Belfast, Ireland, to a Protestant family. His mother died when he was young, and he was raised by his father and private tutors. He displayed exceptional imagination from childhood, creating stories with his brother Warren. In 1908, he attended Campbell College in Belfast, then Malvern College in 1911. During this period, he lost his Christian faith and began questioning religious doctrines. In 1917, he entered Oxford University, but with the outbreak of WWI, he volunteered for the British Army and was sent to the front lines in France.

points.title: 牛津求学与早期创作
points.description: 战后，刘易斯回到牛津大学继续学业，专注于古典文学、哲学和英语文学研究。1924年，他成为牛津大学默顿学院的英语语言和文学讲师。这一时期他与J.R.R.托尔金等学者建立了深厚的友谊，并加入了非正式的文学讨论团体'吉光片羽社'。他开始发表学术论文和诗歌，但尚未转向大众文学创作。1925年，他出版了第一本学术著作《狄更斯：批评研究》，展现了他对文学分析的敏锐洞察力。
points.descriptionEn: After the war, Lewis returned to Oxford to complete his studies, focusing on classics, philosophy, and English literature. In 1924, he became a tutor in English Language and Literature at Magdalen College, Oxford. During this period, he formed deep friendships with scholars like J.R.R. Tolkien and joined the informal literary discussion group 'The Inklings.' He began publishing academic papers and poetry but had not yet turned to popular literary writing. In 1925, he published his first academic work, 'Dymer,' and 'The Pilgrim's Regress,' showing his developing philosophical and literary interests.

points.title: 宗教信仰转变
points.description: 经过长期的哲学思考和理性辩论，刘易斯在1929年重新接受了基督教信仰，这一转变对他后来的创作产生了深远影响。1931年，在托尔金的引导下，他正式皈依基督教。这一信仰转变使他开始探索基督教思想与文学创作的结合。他开始撰写《纯粹的基督教》(1943)，这是一本面向普通读者的基督教信仰入门书籍，后来成为他的代表作之一。这一时期，他还在牛津大学继续教学，同时开始撰写一系列关于文学批评和哲学的著作。
points.descriptionEn: After a long period of philosophical reflection and rational debate, Lewis experienced a religious reversion in 1929, a transformation that profoundly influenced his later writing. Guided by Tolkien, he formally converted to Christianity in 1931. This faith shift led him to explore the integration of Christian thought with literary creation. He began writing 'Mere Christianity' (1943), an introduction to Christian faith for ordinary readers, which became one of his most important works. During this period, he continued teaching at Oxford while beginning to write a series of works on literary criticism and philosophy.

points.title: 纳尼亚传奇创作
points.description: 1950年，刘易斯出版了《纳尼亚传奇》系列的第一部《狮子、女巫和魔衣柜》，这一系列作品成为他最著名的儿童文学创作。1954年，他离开牛津大学，接受剑桥大学中世纪和文艺复兴英语文学的教授职位。这一时期，他完成了《纳尼亚传奇》的全部七部作品，最后一部《最后一战》于1956年出版。这些作品融合了基督教寓言、神话元素和儿童冒险故事，创造了一个深受读者喜爱的奇幻世界。刘易斯通过纳尼亚系列向儿童传达了深刻的道德和宗教观念，同时也展现了他非凡的想象力。
points.descriptionEn: In 1950, Lewis published 'The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe,' the first book in his 'The Chronicles of Narnia' series, which became his most famous children's literary work. In 1954, he left Oxford to accept the position of Professor of Medieval and Renaissance English Literature at Cambridge University. During this period, he completed all seven books of the Narnia series, with the final volume, 'The Last Battle,' published in 1956. These works blended Christian allegory, mythological elements, and children's adventure stories, creating a beloved fantasy world. Through Narnia, Lewis conveyed profound moral and religious concepts to children while showcasing his extraordinary imagination.

points.title: 晚年与遗产
points.description: 1956年，刘易斯与美国作家乔伊·戴维曼结婚，这段婚姻虽然短暂但对他产生了深远影响。乔伊于1960年因癌症去世，刘易斯在悲痛中写下了《悲伤的喜悦》等作品。晚年，他继续在剑桥大学任教，同时进行广泛的写作和演讲。1963年11月22日，刘易斯因肾脏疾病在剑桥去世，同一天，美国总统约翰·肯尼迪也遇刺，导致他的葬礼报道被媒体忽视。刘易斯留下了丰富的文学遗产，包括小说、诗歌、文学批评、宗教著作和书信等，对现代基督教文学和奇幻文学产生了深远影响。
points.descriptionEn: In 1956, Lewis married American writer Joy Davidman, a marriage that, though brief, profoundly affected him. Joy died of cancer in 1960, and Lewis wrote about his grief in works like 'A Grief Observed.' In his later years, he continued teaching at Cambridge while engaging in extensive writing and speaking. On November 22, 1963, Lewis died of kidney disease in Cambridge. His death received little media attention as it coincided with the assassination of President John F. Kennedy. Lewis left behind a vast literary legacy including novels, poetry, literary criticism, religious works, and correspondence, profoundly influencing modern Christian literature and fantasy literature.

appraisal.zh: 刘易斯通常被视为二十世纪最具影响力的基督教思想家之一，其作品把神学思辨与文学表达融为一体，《纳尼亚传奇》既为儿童文学立下新标，也成为传达信仰的媒介。不过也有研究者指出，他笔下的女性角色常处从属地位，非欧洲文化元素被边缘化，其神学整合被认为失之简化，对现代主义文学亦显排斥，这些局限折射出他作为二十世纪中期白人男性知识分子的时代印记。作为吉光片羽社核心成员，他在学术与通俗写作之间架起桥梁，其遗产至今在宗教与流行文化中同时发酵。
appraisal.en: Lewis is generally regarded as one of the most influential Christian thinkers of the twentieth century, fusing theological reflection with literary craft; the Narnia books set new standards for children's literature and served as a vehicle for Christian teaching. Yet other scholars note that his female characters are often subordinate and non-European elements marginalized, that his theological synthesis is judged overly simplified, and that his criticism was dismissive of modernism—limitations reflecting his position as a mid-century white male intellectual. A central figure among the Inklings, he bridged academic and popular writing, and his legacy continues to resonate in both religious and popular culture.

supporter.zh: 支持者视刘易斯为20世纪最具影响力的基督教思想家之一，他的作品将深刻的神学思想与优美的文学表达完美结合。《纳尼亚传奇》系列不仅为儿童文学树立了新标准，也成为传达基督教信仰的有效媒介。他的'纯粹的基督教'著作帮助无数读者重新认识基督教的核心教义。刘易斯通过理性论证和文学创作，成功地将复杂的神学思想转化为普通读者可以理解的形式，对现代基督教护教学和文学创作产生了不可估量的影响。
supporter.en: Supporters view Lewis as one of the most influential Christian thinkers of the 20th century, whose works perfectly combined profound theological insights with beautiful literary expression. The Narnia series not only set new standards for children's literature but also became an effective medium for conveying Christian teachings. His 'Mere Christianity' has helped countless readers rediscover the core doctrines of Christianity. Through rational arguments and literary creation, Lewis successfully transformed complex theological ideas into forms accessible to ordinary readers, exerting immeasurable influence on modern Christian apologetics and literary creation.

critic.zh: 批评者指出刘易斯的作品存在明显的性别和种族偏见，如《纳尼亚传奇》中女性角色常处于从属地位，非欧洲文化元素被边缘化。一些学者认为他的神学思想过于简化，缺乏对复杂神学问题的深入探讨。此外，他的文学批评方法有时被认为过于保守，对现代主义文学持排斥态度。批评者也质疑他在《纯粹的基督教》中对不同基督教传统的整合是否过于表面，未能充分处理各传统间的深刻差异。这些批评反映了刘易斯作为一位20世纪中期白人男性知识分子的历史局限性。
critic.en: Critics point out that Lewis's works exhibit clear gender and racial biases, with female characters often in subordinate positions and non-European cultural elements marginalized in Narnia. Some scholars argue that his theological thought is overly simplified, lacking deep engagement with complex theological issues. Additionally, his literary criticism methods are sometimes considered too conservative, rejecting modernist literature. Critics also question whether his integration of different Christian traditions in 'Mere Christianity' is too superficial, failing to adequately address profound differences between traditions. These criticisms reflect the historical limitations of Lewis as a mid-20th-century white male intellectual.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，刘易斯被定义为一位跨越学术与大众文学边界的多产作家。他的作品既保留了古典文学的严谨性，又具有现代通俗文学的吸引力。作为'吉光片羽社'的核心成员，他与托尔金等人的友谊促进了现代奇幻文学的发展。刘易斯的思想在当代基督教保守派中仍有重要影响，同时他的奇幻作品也吸引了大量非宗教读者。在流行文化中，'纳尼亚传奇'被多次改编为电影、电视剧和舞台剧，成为全球文化现象。刘易斯的一生展现了理性与信仰、学术与创作之间的张力与融合，使他成为20世纪文化史上独特而重要的人物。
objective.en: In academic and popular culture, Lewis is defined as a prolific writer who bridged the boundaries between academic and popular literature. His works maintain the rigor of classical literature while possessing the appeal of modern popular fiction. As a central member of 'The Inklings,' his friendship with Tolkien and others contributed to the development of modern fantasy literature. Lewis's thought remains influential in contemporary Christian conservatism, while his fantasy works also attract numerous non-religious readers. In popular culture, 'The Chronicles of Narnia' has been adapted multiple times into films, TV series, and stage productions, becoming a global cultural phenomenon. Lewis's life demonstrates the tension and integration between reason and faith, academia and creation, making him a unique and significant figure in 20th-century cultural history.

self.zh: 我们通过故事学习，就像我们通过食物生活一样。
self.en: We learn through stories, just as we live through food.
